note: Every external protocol this node speaks, the version we DECLARE, the version that is CURRENT, and the day somebody last checked. Seeded 2026-09-04, the day the gate was written, after a capability audit that was wrong three times in one afternoon: it said the MCP v2 SDK did not exist (it does, as a package split rather than a version bump), that four A2A task states were missing (all eight were produced) and that task results carried no artifacts (they did). Every one of those was a guess where a checked date would have been an answer. Two entries are verified. The rest say untriaged, which is a question nobody has answered and not a clearance: an entry leaves that state by somebody reading the spec and writing what they found, never by re-seeding, which would forgive the whole list at once. `weDeclare` is checked against the code on every commit, so the ledger cannot drift from what the node actually says; `verifiedOn` is checked against maxAgeDays, so the ledger cannot go quietly stale.

verdicts.current: We declare what is current. Nothing to do.
verdicts.watch: A newer revision exists and we have decided not to move yet. The note says why and what would change the answer.
verdicts.adopt: We have decided to move. The note says what is left.
verdicts.decline: A newer revision exists and we will not follow it. The note says what we do instead.
verdicts.untriaged: Nobody has compared what we declare against what is current. Not a clearance.

protocols.name: Model Context Protocol
protocols.note: Two revisions behind, and the newer one is a rework rather than an increment: sessions and the initialize handshake are gone, `server/discover` is mandatory, `subscriptions/listen` replaces resources/subscribe, and Roots, Sampling and Logging are deprecated. Measured on branch mcp-v2-prototype against the real catalogue: all 306 published tools register on @modelcontextprotocol/server 2.0.0 unchanged, server/discover answers, a stateless request works, and a client on 2025-06-18 is still served by the same handler. So the move is viable and not urgent. What would change the answer: the SDK settling (maintainers are limiting PRs while v2 beds in), or a client we care about requiring the newer revision. NOTE the two declaration sites — this version is written out twice, and the gate checks both because one of them has been forgotten before.

protocols.name: Agent2Agent
protocols.note: We serve 1.x through @a2a-js/sdk (A2A_PROTOCOL_VERSION) and declare 0.3 BESIDE it, deliberately: almost every client in the world still speaks 0.3, the SDK ships the compatibility layer, and the card declares both interfaces so a client reading either finds an address. The value tracked here is the legacy one, because it is the one written out by hand. Surface as of 2026-09-04: streaming on, push notifications on, extended agent card on, all eight task states produced, artifacts on the task, x402 extension declared.

protocols.name: x402 machine payments
protocols.note: Nobody has checked whether x402 has moved past version 1. We serve /.well-known/x402.json on base-sepolia with the facilitator at x402.org, non-custodial, per-item 402s.

protocols.name: OpenAPI
protocols.note: 3.2 exists. Nobody has read what it would give us. Separately and worth its own look: the served document is 1.6 MB, which is large enough that at least one agent-readiness scanner times out reading it and reports it as invalid JSON.

protocols.name: Agentic Commerce Protocol
protocols.note: Served at /.well-known/acp.json. Nobody has compared it against the published spec.

protocols.name: Universal Commerce Profile
protocols.note: Served at /.well-known/ucp. Nobody has compared it against the published spec.

protocols.name: WebMCP
protocols.note: Manifest at /.well-known/webmcp.json, library at /v1/libs/aimeat-webmcp.js. Form tool annotations are not implemented.

protocols.name: Web Bot Auth
protocols.note: Signatures directory at /.well-known/http-message-signatures-directory. A draft that moves; nobody has followed it.

protocols.name: Agent Skills
protocols.note: Index served; skill.md carries YAML frontmatter. Nobody has checked the convention against its source.

protocols.name: llms.txt
protocols.note: Scored 100 on llmstxt.org compliance by an external scanner on 2026-09-04, which is not the same as somebody having read the spec.

protocols.name: OASF agent records
protocols.note: Projection served at /v1/oasf/:owner/:agent. Directory listing was deferred until agents describe what they sell.

protocols.name: Agentic Resource Discovery
protocols.note: NOT IMPLEMENTED. /.well-known/ai-catalog.json is 404 and no Agentmap directive, link tag or DNS record points anywhere. A decision, not an oversight: wish-ard-ai-catalog in the wish bucket carries the analysis and the two open questions.

protocols.name: OAuth Protected Resource Metadata (RFC 9728)
protocols.note: Two documents served: the origin's at the bare well-known path and the MCP endpoint's at the path-suffixed one, fixed 2026-09-04 after a scanner found the apex naming a resource it was not. The RFC itself has not been re-read since.

protocols.name: OAuth Device Authorization Grant (RFC 8628)
protocols.note: How every agent gets an identity here. Stable RFC, but nobody has checked our flow against it since it was written.

protocols.name: agents.txt
protocols.note: Served at /agents.txt. A young convention with no settled owner; nobody has checked whose version we follow.
